correctness.rationale: Constructed the four exact adjacency models from the formulas and verified the supplied root-to-vertex automorphisms and every spanning path witness against these graphs. Positives only require one root because the automorphisms carry the vertex, its opposite class, and each path together. Independently enumerated simple paths recursively, without the submitted subset DP or transitivity reduction, for every starting vertex in the full graph and every deletion and admissible endpoint pair. In H,M,P,D order this checked 98,128,162,200 ordered full cases, all positive, and 294,448,648,900 punctured pairs, with 0,16,0,0 failures. The 16 failures give one per M deletion, precisely the unique original-graph distance-(3,3,4) pair by BFS. For deletion 0, its ends are 10,14. Each of 1,7,8 must use both remaining incident edges; the unused edges therefore have degrees one at the other ten vertices and two at 10,14 in the 15-edge induced graph. Enumerating seven-edge subsets finds six possible unused-edge sets; the residual components have sizes (5,10) or (6,9), three cases each. This corroborates the source obstruction, including its claim of exactly two components. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_discrete.py.
residual_risks: The submitted C++ final guard alone would not reject all possible nonzero defect counts in the three non-Möbius–Kantor graphs; the compiled output records zero, and the independently verified explicit witnesses and direct exhaustive search directly establish zero.
Conclusion applies only to the four graphs and one deleted vertex. Neither graph isomorphism classification beyond the four specified adjacency models nor multi-fault tolerance was audited.

Pensaert Theorem 2 as contrast with ordinary laceability
value.rationale: A natural complete finite classification on the four already distinguished cubic symmetric girth-six graphs. The result resolves a stronger extension property than ordinary Hamilton laceability and gives an intrinsic, unique, checkable witness explaining why the Möbius–Kantor case differs. The endpoint-level characterization provides useful data for comparing fault tolerance without relying on vertex labels or an unmotivated graph slice.
residual_risks: The theorem does not identify a general characterization for other cubic symmetric graphs or a threshold for multiple faults.
